I’m choosing local identification of restoring-force couplings in an assembled material as the next principal direction. The useful operation is to distinguish a direct mechanical interaction from correlated motion produced by the surrounding structure. That distinction matters when deciding whether to change a chemical bond, alter its environment, or revise the material model used to predict an intervention.

There is now a substantive theoretical result, a discriminating construction, and an initial physical test. The proposed observable contains the desired information. Two ordinary overlapping electron probes do not yet isolate it. The unresolved interface is consequently quite specific.

The earlier mass witness, returned mediator, static-label comparison and withdrawn small-motif justification retain their previous scope. None of the calculations below upgrades isotope identification, survival, transfer chemistry or beamtime estimates.

Recent experiments provide a particularly relevant starting point. Atomic-scale electron interferometry has measured directional vibrational correlations between adjacent silicon columns. Its interpretation uses an effective harmonic-chain model that incorporates the surrounding crystal through an on-site restraint. That is a substantial realised capability and the closest comparator for this opening.
